tagline.text: The Philippines' deepest lake, with a sulfur hot spring and wintering birds

location.label: Location
location.text: Around Kitcharao and Jabonga in Agusan del Norte, and Mainit and Alegria in Surigao del Norte

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱500~1,500 (day trip from Butuan, transport included)

children.text: Lake Mainit lies between Agusan del Norte and Surigao del Norte and is the deepest lake in the Philippines. Three things bring visitors here: views from the lakeside highway, the sulfur hot spring at Mapaso, and a winter haven for migratory birds.

Lake Mainit sits in northeastern Mindanao, on a narrow plain between mountain ranges in the Caraga region. It straddles the boundary of Agusan del Norte and Surigao del Norte; Mainit and Alegria stand on the Surigao del Norte shore, and Kitcharao and Jabonga on the Agusan del Norte shore. According to Wikipedia the surface area is about
170 km²
(some survey sources give about 140 km²), making it the fourth-largest lake in the country. The surface elevation is about
(some sources give 27 m).
Depth is what makes this lake special. The maximum depth is about

, and it is known as the deepest lake in the Philippines. The shoreline drops away steeply, so the water gets deep very quickly a short way from the bank. At least 14 small rivers and streams flow into the lake, and its only outlet is the Kalinawan River, which runs south through Pagusi Lake and the Tubay River to Butuan Bay.

The name is said to come from the Visayan word mainit, meaning hot. Hot springs are said to feed the lake, and north of Mainit town you can find the sulfur-spring Mapaso Wellness Resort. Being able to combine the lake and a hot spring in a single day is a big advantage of coming here.

That said, Lake Mainit is not a resort destination like Cebu or Boracay. Do not expect lake cruises or polished viewing decks; it is first of all a working lake for local fishers. It suits travelers with some time to spare who want to add quiet lake scenery and a hot spring on the way to or from Butuan or Surigao. Tourism development around the lake is still at the planning stage, so check local conditions before you visit.
The maximum depth is known to be about
, and the average depth is about
. The water looks dark and calm and is hard to tell apart from a shallow lake at first glance, but once you know it grows deeper toward the middle, the view feels different.

blocks.title: Lake views from the Kitcharao highway

children.text: On the national highway running north from Butuan, the lake opens up in front of you around Kitcharao. Travel bloggers name this stretch as the best place to see it. There are not many places to stop the car, so pick a safe shoulder and take a short break.

blocks.title: Hot spring at Mapaso Wellness Resort

children.text: This local-government-run sulfur hot spring lies about
2 km
from Mainit town. It has several pools fed by continuously flowing water, and the sulfur stains the pool walls rust-red. The entrance fee is low, so it is a good way to rest after a day at the lake.

Local travelers say sunrise is best seen from the Jabonga side and sunset from San Roque in Kitcharao. Because of the mountain ranges on the east of the lake and the plain on the west, the best spot changes with the time of day. If your schedule allows, staying long at one place is also a good choice.

blocks.title: A winter haven for migratory birds

children.text: The lake is regarded as an important wetland on the East Asian-Australasian Flyway. Asian Waterbird Census averages for 2019–2021 recorded about 33,000 Tufted Ducks, which makes it the largest wintering site in the Philippines. Ducks, herons, egrets, shorebirds, and terns are also seen.

About 41 species of fish, 5 crustaceans, and 8 mollusks have been reported in the lake. Villagers catch and sell fish such as pijanga (tank goby) and buguan, and you can see fishers using the traditional boat cast net (laya) along the shore.

The forests around the lake have a high share of endemic plants and are recognized as a Key Biodiversity Area (KBA). The watershed also hosts Rafflesia mixta, a rare plant described only recently. It is interesting that the ecosystem runs unbroken from lake to forest.
In Butuan, get on a
bus or van bound for Surigao
or rent a car and set out. Follow the national highway north.
Pass Jabonga and Cabadbaran; when the lake begins to appear around Kitcharao, stop at a safe spot and take photos of the whole lake.
Continue toward Mainit town. If you are on a bus, tell the conductor in advance to let you off at the
Magpayang junction
From the junction, take a tricycle or a motorcycle taxi (habal-habal) to Mapaso Wellness Resort. On arrival, check the condition and temperature of the pools.
Enjoy the hot spring and eat the packed lunch you brought. There are almost no restaurants, so bring water and food in advance.
Take one more look at the lake from Mainit town, then catch a bus back toward Surigao or Butuan.
Bus times and road conditions change often, so be sure to ask the staff at the Butuan terminal for the last bus time from the Mainit side.
Arrive in Mainit town, drop your bags at a lakeside lodge, and stroll along the shore watching fishers cast their nets.
Head to the lake around dusk for sunset. Take your time watching the sun go down over the water.
Go to Mapaso hot spring early for a quiet soak.
If you have time, visit the Jabonga side of the lakeshore, which is said to be good for sunrise. It is some distance away and you will need a vehicle.
Lodging near the lake is limited. Places such as Mainit Kasili Lakeside Resort have been described on blogs, but check directly whether they are still operating.
Cebu Pacific and Philippine Airlines group carriers fly nonstop from Manila (MNL) to Butuan Bancasi Airport (BXU). The flight takes about
1 hour 45 minutes
From the airport, take a tricycle or taxi to the Butuan city bus terminal, then board a bus toward Surigao.
Fares and flight frequencies vary a lot by season, so check on the airline's official app.
You can also fly into Surigao Sayak Airport (SUG), but check the latest information on whether Manila flights are operating.
Take a bus toward Surigao from the Butuan bus terminal and get off at Magpayang in Mainit. Ask the staff before departure to make sure it is not a non-stop bus.
The road distance from Butuan to Surigao is about
120 km
, the bus takes about
2.5–3 hours
, and the fare is known to be about ₱245~303. Mainit lies along the way, so the time is shorter than that.
One travel blog records that it took about
2 hours
from Butuan to Magpayang.
From Surigao City, take a bus heading south toward Butuan and get off at Mainit. Mainit is described as about
1 hour
from Surigao City.
Some travelers arrive in Surigao by boat from Siargao or Dinagat and then come over to Mainit.
From the Magpayang junction to Mapaso hot spring, use a tricycle or a motorcycle taxi. Blog records show the tricycle at about
per person and the motorcycle taxi at about
round trip.
Parts of the road are unpaved and slippery in the rain, so agree on the price with the local driver beforehand.
The Caraga region has no clear dry season, and rain is heaviest in winter (roughly December to February). For viewing the lake and soaking in an outdoor hot spring, the less rainy months are better.
If you want to see migratory birds, you can aim for the period when winter birds arrive. However, the weather varies greatly, so check the forecast before you leave.

There are not many places to stay around the lake the way there are in tourist spots. One or two lakeside resorts in Mainit town are described on blogs, so confirm that they are operating by phone or map-app reviews before booking. If options are few, it is easier to base yourself in Butuan or Surigao and make a day trip.

Food near the lake is limited. Mapaso hot spring is said to have almost no restaurants, so bring a packed meal and water. Locals enjoy the lake fish pijanga, so ask at a local eatery what is on the menu.
If the hot spring is your goal, choose a dry day and go early in the morning if possible. It may be crowded around midday.
On the bus, be sure to ask to be dropped at the Magpayang junction. If you pass it, it is hard to come back.
Bring a towel and a change of clothes for a cold shower after the spring. The changing stalls are simple.
Lake photos come out much better in the early morning or at dusk than at midday.
Parts of the road are unpaved, so motorcycle taxis may be slower after rain. Leave extra time.
Carry plenty of cash in pesos. There are few ATMs in the villages.
Mobile signal can be weak along parts of the lakeshore, so download an offline map.
Keep your distance from the birds and fishers even when you get close, and do not throw trash into the lake.
Tourism development around the lake is only just being discussed, and facility and security information changes often, so check with the local government and recent local news before you leave.
Hot spring fees and hours differ between sources and many are old. Confirm them locally.
The spring contains sulfur, so people with sensitive skin, pregnant women, and anyone with a weak heart should be careful. Medical benefits have not been officially verified.
A hydroelectric plant has operated on the lake since 2023, and it has been pointed out that this may change the water level. Keep an eye on the shoreline water level.
Water pollution from farming, mining, and logging has been reported in the watershed. Follow local advice about swimming in the lake or eating its fish.
A survey report also lists security in the wetland area as a risk factor, so avoid traveling remote roads late at night and check the latest travel advisories.
This is the main city of Agusan, on the way up to Lake Mainit. It is the gateway by plane from Manila, and the road runs overland from the airport to the lake.
A surfing island reached by boat from Surigao City. You can combine it with Lake Mainit in a single Caraga itinerary.
A group of islands reached by boat from Surigao. They make a natural follow-up island trip after the lake.
